name: Fiducial & Tooling Planner
blurb: fiducial and tooling-hole placement for assembly
intro: Where the global fiducials and tooling holes go on a board or on its panel rails, with their clear areas. Sizes follow IPC-7351B / SMEMA 3.1 (1-3 mm copper dot, clear area one diameter all round); the edge and hole distances are common assembler rules of thumb.

inputs.label: Rail width
inputs.help: Only used for rails. 5 mm is common; the rails run along X, top and bottom.

inputs.label: Fiducial diameter
inputs.help: Bare copper dot, no mask on it. 1.0 mm is what most assemblers ask for.

inputs.label: Clear area diameter
inputs.help: Mask opening and keep-out: no copper, silk or parts. At least 3x the dot.

inputs.label: Fiducial centre from edge
inputs.help: On the board: keep the clear area out of the ~3 mm the conveyor grips.

inputs.label: Tooling hole diameter
inputs.help: Non-plated. Ask the assembler: 2.0, 3.0 and 3.2 mm are common.

inputs.label: Fine-pitch parts (≤0.5 mm, BGA)
inputs.help: Each gets two local fiducials on its diagonal.

examples.title: 80 x 50 mm board, fiducials on the board
Small 30 x 20 mm board on 5 mm rails

usage: Give the board size in mm and whether the marks go on the board or on panel rails; fiducial and tooling-hole sizes in mm. It returns the X/Y coordinates (origin bottom-left of the board, or of the panel when on rails) of every global fiducial and tooling hole with their keep-out diameters, the fiducial spans, the local fiducial count, and warnings when a mark does not fit, sits in the conveyor edge, or overlaps another. Use it before placement so the marks are in the layout from the start.
sources: IPC-7351B section 3.4 (fiducial size 1.0-3.0 mm, clear area of twice the radius)
Assembler rules of thumb: 3-5 mm conveyor edge, fiducials as far apart as possible and not symmetric
